liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Standing on the Moon** (3 reviews): Attendee recalls Standing on the Moon bringing back strong memories of seeing the show with a high school sweetheart; Up-tempo Standing on the Moon: drummers tried at least twice to slow Jerry before giving in to his tempo [15][16][18]
- **Here Comes Sunshine** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opening Here Comes Sunshine great, leading into a tight first set [14]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer describes China Cat as fast and fun [14]
- **New Speedway Boogie** (1 review): Reviewer notes Jerry playing slide on New Speedway Boogie, which the reviewer never heard him do before [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil practices base line by himself**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **it would really help to have Vinny here...Bob did you give that disc to Steve?**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **mostly dead air, drummers start to come in**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **Phil, Vince, and drummers practice**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **Phil gives directions**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **Vince- Let me here the groove of the body of the song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **Let's do the verses from A-Minor C - Take 1**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **more from the A-minor C - Take 2**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd95-03-17.soundcheck.sbd.17951.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 28 songs; 43 min; rated 3.25/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundcheck recording is flat, short on bass and stereo separation, apparently an ear-monitor feed [13]
- **gd1995-03-17.142982.Boedicker.flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd95-03-17.sbd.16057.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 164 min; rated 2.9/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: The soundboard matrix is crisp and enjoyable, unlike audience tapes at the Spectrum, which tend to be poor and bass-heavy [14]
- **gd1995-03-17.aud.bleich.91840.flac16**: audience recording; 18 songs; 166 min [6]. Said about its sound: Audience source with occasional low-end oversaturation that was attenuated; tape flips are crossfaded and EQ applied [6]

## Around the show

- Soundcheck tape captures the band rehearsing Unbroken Chain and Here Comes Sunshine; Garcia appears only near the end, Phil mostly instructing [13]
- Attendee remembers Jerry using a teleprompter onstage to help with lyrics [17]
- Phil sings a lot with loud vocals, seemingly warming up for Unbroken Chain two nights later [18]
- Reviewer claims Phil can be heard near the end of the soundcheck asking Jerry about changing his songs; no audible reply [20]
- Weir played acoustic on Eternity; several takes of Unbroken Chain were done during soundcheck rehearsal [2]
- Reviewer finds Garcia nearly absent and sloppy, with a choppy band; the next night is judged possibly the best of Spring 95 [19]
- Reviewer regards the rehearsal as coming too late, leading to a disappointing Unbroken Chain breakout [20]
- Reviewer found these 1995 shows less compelling than mid-to-late 1980s Spectrum shows [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd95-03-17.soundcheck.sbd.17951.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Rehersal - Phil's Ear Monitor Feed > Crew Member's Cassette Master (recorded inside venue) > 2nd Gen Cassette **see notes via Marc Pujol [1]. Also: Transferred from second-generation cassette via Kenwood deck and RME interface at 96kHz/24bit, with slight hiss reduction, then converted to 44.1/16 SHN [1]
- **gd1995-03-17.142982.Boedicker.flac1644**: taped by Dave Boedicker; transferred by Dave Boedicker; source: Source:Nakamichi 300 Mics W/CP4 Shotguns>Marantz PMD 430 Cassette Deck>Maxell XL-II-S Cassette Masters(1 90 Minute; Tape,1 100 Minute Tape)>Dolby "B" On>Sony… [2]. Also: A tape flip falls after Lazy River Road, with no music lost going into Eternity [2]
- **gd95-03-17.sbd.16057.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sources: Primary - DSBD >?>Bootleg CD>EAC>SHN.Secondary audience source (Schoeps MK4) used for drums > space.This source represents a composite of the two… [3]
- **gd1995-03-17.aud.bleich.91840.flac16**: taped by John Bleich; transferred by B. Green; source: Nak 300's > D6 > Master Cassette > DR-3 > Emu 1212M > 24/96 Wav > Wavelab 5 > Plugings > R8 Brain > 32/44.1 Wave > L3 > 16/44.1 Wave > Flac Lvl 8 (TLH) [6]. Also: Source tapes supplied by John Bleich; transfer and edit by Bgreen [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [GRATEFUL DEAD 1995-03-17 Fri Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1250056778020/grateful-dead-1995-03-17-fri-spectrum) [26]
- Poster by kempepedia.blogspot.com: [It Was 20 Years Ago Today: Grateful Dead, March 17th and 18th, 1995, The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA](https://kempepedia.blogspot.com/2015/03/it-was-20-years-ago-today-grateful-dead.html) [27]
- Poster by gravitystereo: [Grateful Dead - First Night At The Spectrum ( 2 CD SET ) ( The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA, March 17th, 1995 ) - gravitys](https://gravitystereo.com/product/grateful-dead-first-night-at-the-spectrum-2-cd-set-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-march-17th-1995/) [28]
